messages:
ashok: apac-east dedicated pool showing tail latency spikes on small inference jobs since ~02:10 UTC. CPU and GPU util look normal but p99 token latency jumps to ~600ms from 120ms.
maya: any recurring pattern? time of day / tenant? :thinking:
julia: I saw similar on our canary a few mins ago. looks correlated with high egress bursts from a single tenant (tenant-id t-42).
kevin: logs show a lot of NIC retransmits and high tx-queue stalls on the host. suspect noisy egress impacting kernel softirq handling -> stall propagation to GPU driver.
ashok: repro log snip:
```
[netdev]: tx-queue 3 backlog 12456 pkts
kernel: softirq=high cpu=2
ndev: tx_qsz=512 drops=216
```
maya: interesting — we've seen this before with model-parallel batchers that send lots of small requests. Could be packet-spray causing IRQ saturation on the host.
julia: can we move t-42 out of the apac-east dedicated slice temporarily? or throttle egress on tenant policer?
kevin: quick mitigation: apply egress policer to t-42 (10 Mbps) and move their allocs to a different AZ rack to test if p99 recovers.
ops-bot: action scheduled: applied policer to tenant t-42 (rule id pol-781). Monitoring p99 for 10m.
maya: after policer p99 dropped to ~140ms within 2 minutes. good sign.
ashok: long-term we should add a routing constraint: prefer apac-west for heavy-egress tenants when host NIC softirq ratio > X. basically a fallback routing policy based on NIC health signal.
julia: +1. Also consider a proactive detection: if we see sustained tx-queue>threshold, mark host as egress-shield and steer new allocs away.
kevin: question: what's the cost tradeoff vs dedicated pool churn? moving tenants around increases backfill churn and may hurt packing efficiency.
maya: rough calc: moving one noisy tenant off a 16-GPU dedicated slice reduces SLO breaches but increases backfill churn by ~0.6 GPU-hours/day. cost still lower than SLA penalties for customers.
ashok: proposal: implement two-step playbook:
1) short-term: auto-apply policer + soft-evict to sibling AZ for the tenant (fast path).
2) long-term: scheduler signal - host-egress-health => routing preference weight to avoid that AZ for heavy-egress tenants for 30m.
julia: agree. can we add a telemetry flag for hosts showing NIC softirq>20% and tx-queue>8k? that'll drive the scheduler weight.
kevin: I'll open a PR for the policer automation + telemetry metric. tagging @maya @julia for review.
maya: SGTM. after PR+canary we should run a synthetic burst test to validate no regressions for warm-pool behavior.
ashok: thanks all. follow-up: if policer doesn't help in 15m we'll initiate full tenant migration and open an incident.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2028 (tail-latency-apac-east). responders: ashok, maya, kevin, julia.
